explain.say: Look at the first dot. In 1947, scientists at Bell Labs in the USA invented the transistor, a tiny switch that turns electricity on and off with no moving parts. Computers count with on and off, which we write as 1 and 0. How many switches do you think your phone has? Billions!

explain.say: Look at these bars. In 1995 about 16 million people used the internet. By 2024 it was about 5.5 billion, two in every three people on Earth. Amazing work! Here is a challenge: about 2.6 billion people are still offline. How could we connect them?

items.ask: How many people use the internet?

faq.a: A tiny electronic switch that can turn a current on and off, or make it stronger. Invented at Bell Labs in 1947, transistors are the building blocks of every computer chip, which today can hold billions of them.
An early computer network funded by the US Department of Defense. On 29 October 1969 it sent its first message between computers at UCLA and Stanford. It grew into the internet.
A computer's central brain on a single chip. The first one sold, the Intel 4004 in 1971, had about 2,300 transistors; modern chips have billions.

faq.q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
faq.a: British scientist Tim Berners-Lee invented it at CERN, near Geneva, proposing it in 1989 and launching the first website in 1991. The web runs on the internet, which is the network underneath.
asks: Is the web the same as the internet?

faq.q: How many people use the internet?
faq.a: About 5.5 billion people in 2024, around two thirds of the world, according to the International Telecommunication Union. About 2.6 billion people are still offline, mostly in poorer and rural areas.

facts: The transistor was invented at Bell Labs in 1947.
The Intel 4004, released in 1971, had about 2,300 transistors.
About 5.5 billion people used the internet in 2024, according to the ITU.
